title: The IKEA Effect

scenes.text: Why do you love the wobbly shelf *you* built?
scenes.vo: Why do you love that slightly wobbly shelf you built yourself?

scenes.text: Researchers asked people to build plain IKEA boxes
scenes.vo: Researchers asked people to assemble plain IKEA storage boxes.

scenes.text:
Builders would pay
*63% more* for their own box
scenes.vo: The builders were willing to pay about 63 percent more for their box than others paid for an identical pre-built one.
This is the IKEA effect. When we put effort into something, we overvalue it.

scenes.text: The catch: it only works if you *finish*
scenes.vo: The catch: the effect disappeared when people didn't finish, or built it and then took it apart.

scenes.text:
“Build your own” products.
Your own ideas in meetings.
scenes.vo: It's why build-your-own products sell, and why we defend our own ideas a little too hard.

scenes.text: Ask: do I love the idea, or the *effort* I put in?
scenes.vo: So ask yourself: do I love this idea, or just the effort I put into it?

scenes.text:
Follow *@inquisitive_bytes*
for a daily byte of behaviour science
scenes.vo: Follow Inquisitive Bytes for a daily byte of behaviour science.

caption:
Effort makes things feel more valuable, even flat-pack boxes. 🛠️ It's called the IKEA effect.

What's something you made that you secretly know isn't that good? 😅👇
source: Norton, M. I., Mochon, D. & Ariely, D. (2012). The IKEA effect: When labor leads to love. Journal of Consumer Psychology, 22(3).
